stem:
Vihaan asks whether $83$ can be a perfect square.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Call $83$ a perfect-square label rather than a number checked by its last digit.
Being a perfect square is what produces a forbidden units digit, so the digit test runs backwards from the square claim.
No: a perfect square cannot end in $3$, so $83$ is not a perfect square.
Reject $83$ only because the printed tens digit $8$ looks even.

teacher.key_rationale: Perfect squares end only in 0,1,4,5,6,9; ending in 3 rules 83 out. Naming it a label swaps the test. Saying squareness produces the digit reverses the digit rule. Focusing on tens digit 8 captures a surface cue.
